newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-AUSSIE DLR STILL IN FIGHT FOR US$0.7400.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-AUSSIE DLR STILL IN FIGHT FOR US$0.7400.

text.p: *Australian dollar manages break towards US$0.7420, but pushed lower as RBA governor Macfarlane's speech seen leaving room for further rate cuts.
*Buying appears on dip lower, and dollar recovers to US$0.74 level that it was strongly rebuffed at on Tuesday, in line with expectations that dollar remains in broad US$0.7300/7450 range.
The Australian dollar was attempting to gain a solid foothold at US$0.7400, having been rebuffed at or above that level twice in the last 24 hours.
The dollar had risen to a week high of US$0.7421 in European trade ahead of a speech by RBA governor Ian Macfarlane that was expected to be bullish for the unit.
Instead the dollar fell to its lows after the speech, which was not as hawkish in its rate outlook as some had expected.
By early trade, however, the dollar had recovered from its lows and at 8.00 a.m. (2200 GMT) was trading at US$0.7401/06, up on Tuesday's local close of US$0.7391/96.
While Macfarlane was bullish on the growth outlook, saying growth above 4.5 percent was possible in the next few years, he said it was the inflation outlook that determined rate changes.

"We have an inflation target, appropriately and flexibly defined, which tells us to tighten when our forecast of inflation has it exceeding the target for any sustained period of time, and to ease when the forecast has inflation sustainably below target," Macfarlane said.
Given Australia's favourable inflation outlook, traders saw that as a sign that rates were on hold for some time, with another easing still a possibility.
The two interest rate easings this year, and the prospect of more, have been a key factor behind the Australian dollar's five month downtrend from March's high just above US$0.80.

However, the dollar showed resolve to find good support at US$0.7370 and returning to make another attempt at US$0.7400. An attempt at this level on Tuesday provoked some large Asian selling, so the market was cautious to push ahead agressively.

Macfarlane also said that given the different cyclical poistion of the U.S. and Australian economies, and lower local inflation, it was "entirely fit and proper" that Australian rates out to five years were below U.S. rates.
With no local data of note scheduled for Wednesday, the dollar was not expected to make any significant moves and should remain comfortably within its broader US$0.7300/7450 range
On the crosses, a stronger U.S. dollar saw the Australian dollar extend Tuesday's gains. The dollar opened at 86.12/22 yen and 1.3799/3812 marks from local closes of 85.81/91 and 1.3777/90.
